results.title: How to Test Edge Cases and Boundary Conditions in Unit Tests
results.content: However, unit testing can be challenging when it comes to testing edge cases and boundary conditions, which are scenarios that occur at the extremes or limits of the input, output, or logic of the unit. In this article, you will learn how to test edge cases and boundary conditions in unit tests for different languages and platforms. Testing edge cases and boundary conditions can help you identify and prevent potential bugs, errors, or failures in your unit. Edge cases and boundary conditions are scenarios in software testing that focus on the extreme or limit values of input parameters. Testing edge cases and boundary conditions in unit tests involves identifying the extreme values and limits within the input domain and creating test cases specifically targeting these scenarios. By systematically incorporating edge cases and boundary conditions into your unit testing strategy, you can identify and address potential vulnerabilities in your software.

results.title: Virtual Beings | **Sign Language Translation System Animates 3D Avatar Using HamNoSys Encoding and WebGL Rendering ** | Facebook
results.content: Arabic Algerian sign language translation system. Summarized by AI from the post below. **Sign Language Translation System Animates 3D Avatar Using HamNoSys Encoding and WebGL Rendering**. The technical infrastructure of the Arabic Algerian Sign Language (ALSL) translation system centers on a pipeline that converts written Arabic into animated 3D sign language gestures performed by a digital avatar. At the heart of the system is the use of HamNoSys (Hamburg Notation System) to encode sign gestures, which are then translated into SiGML (Signing Gesture Markup Language), a machine-readable XML format. This SiGML data is used to animate the avatar through the CWASA system (CWA Signing Avatars), which renders the avatar's movements using WebGL and JavaScript. The avatar itself is a rigged 3D model capable of nuanced, lifelike gestures, including facial expressions and body postures required for authentic sign language. Supporting components include the eSIGN editor for dictionary building, the CWASA SigML Player for animation playback, and a user interface designed around CWASA to input text and view signed output.

results.title: Any idea on how to write unit tests for a Pratt parser? : r/ProgrammingLanguages
results.content: I would consider property-based testing in the following way: (1) generate a random syntax tree, (2) serialize the syntax tree into code in your language, (3) parse the serialized code with your parser, (4) check that the parsed tree is equivalent to the initially generated one. By the way, I mentioned how to test the parser with property based testing, but you could also use it to test the bytecode compiler and VM itself by implementing a syntax tree interpreter (as simple as possible, efficiency is not the goal here, correctness is), and then run generated programs (or syntax trees) in the VM as well as in the interpreter and check that the outputs are the same.

results.title: Can Claude Code help write unit tests?
results.content: * Can Claude Code help write unit tests? # Can Claude Code help write unit tests? Claude Code excels at writing comprehensive unit tests and is considered by many developers to be one of its most valuable capabilities. When generating tests, Claude Code understands the context of your existing codebase, follows your project’s testing conventions, and can write tests in the appropriate testing framework for your language, whether that’s Jest for JavaScript, pytest for Python, JUnit for Java, or other testing frameworks. The test generation process with Claude Code is intelligent and context-aware, going beyond simple happy-path testing to include comprehensive coverage scenarios. For example, when testing a payment processing function, Claude Code might generate tests for successful payments, failed payments, network timeouts, invalid input data, boundary conditions like zero amounts or maximum values, and security scenarios like injection attempts. You can ask Claude Code to write tests based on expected input/output pairs before implementing functionality, ensuring that tests fail initially as expected in TDD methodology, then implement code to make those tests pass.
